title: Martin wins French GP Sprint as Marquez fails to finish
snippet: Martin wins French GP Sprint as Marquez fails to finish. Jorge Martin wins 2026 MotoGP Sprint Race in France. By Andrew Clarke. Date posted: 10 May 2026. Jorge
extractedText: Martin wins French GP Sprint as Marquez fails to finishBy Andrew ClarkeDate posted: 9 May 2026Jorge Martin charged from eighth on the grid to win the MotoGP French Grand Prix Sprint at Le Mans on Saturday, with polesitter Francesco Bagnaia second and championship leader Marco Bezzecchi third. Martin crossed the line for Aprilia Racing in 19m46.830s, 1.107 seconds ahead of Bagnaia, with Bezzecchi a further 1.679 seconds back to complete an Aprilia front row lockout on the rostrum. The result was a blow for Ducati Lenovo Team, with Marc Marquez failing to finish after qualifying second and setting a new lap record in Q1 earlier in the day. Bagnaia denies Marquez in qualifying The qualifying hour had belonged to Bagnaia and Marquez. Marquez shattered the Le Mans lap record in Q1 to progress into Q2 alongside Fabio Quartararo, who delivered for the home crowd to take the second transfer spot. In Q2, Marquez charged to provisional pole on his second run before Bagnaia produced a final flying lap to deny his teammate. It was Bagnaia’s first pole of the season and his first since Sepang last year, with the pair forming a Ducati Lenovo Team front row for the first time since Brno last year. Bezzecchi grabbed the final front row position to complete a strong afternoon for the Aprilia camp. Martin makes his move The Sprint told a different story. Martin, starting eighth, moved forward quickly and was among the leaders when it mattered. Bagnaia held on for second to collect nine points, while Bezzecchi’s third place extended his advantage at the top of the championship standings. Pedro Acosta was fourth for Red Bull KTM Factory Racing ahead of Quartararo, who backed up a solid qualifying display with fifth place and more valuable points for Monster Energy Yamaha MotoGP. Joan Mir took sixth for Honda HRC Castrol, the best result among the Honda runners. Ai Ogura was seventh for Trackhouse MotoGP ahead of Alex Marquez, who recovered from a Q2 crash at Turn 3 to finish eighth. Diogo Moreira took ninth for Pro Honda LCR ahead of Johann Zarco, with the home crowd finding something to cheer from the local rider’s top 10 finish. Australian Jack Miller crossed 15th for Prima Pramac Yamaha MotoGP. Marquez among the retirements Marc Marquez was among several riders who failed to finish, along with Raul Fernandez, Franco Morbidelli, Enea Bastianini, Jonas Folger and Luca Marini.
